clue.text: Cost of docking off the Dorset coast?

definitions.text: Cost of docking off the Dorset coast?

parts.words: Cost of docking off the Dorset coast?
parts.note: read playfully, the charge for bringing a ship into harbour and stepping ashore becomes the name of a headland on the south coast of England

explanation.surface: A sailor queries the mooring fee charged somewhere off the coast of Dorset.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is a pun: a port fee and a landing bill run together to name a real place. Dorset is a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a narrow rocky promontory at the southern tip of the Isle of Portland in Dorset, famous for its lighthouse.

clue.text: Punishment not applicable in the case of coppers

indicators.note: read literally, one piece is put inside the casing formed by the other

parts.note: coppers are low-value copper coins, pennies
NA is the standard abbreviation for not applicable on forms

explanation.surface: No penalty applies where police officers are concerned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' suggests police but means the coins; 'in the case of' looks like a phrase meaning 'regarding' but puts NA inside PENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is self-imposed suffering or a sanction undertaken to atone for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Involving a lean, down-to-earth fellow

parts.note: re means concerning or involving, as in business letters
to list is to lean over, as a ship does

explanation.surface: Something involving a thin, practical man.
explanation.definitionFit: A practical person who faces facts as they are rather than idealising them.

clue.text: Sweetener for sweetbread initially

parts.note: a sweetener is named by splitting sweetbread into sweet and bread, and putting the bread first

explanation.surface: A cook adds something sugary to sweetbreads at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweetbreads are offal, but here the word splits into SWEET (SUGAR) and BREAD (LOAF), with 'initially' putting the bread first.
explanation.definitionFit: Refined cane product formerly sold as a solid cone or block, from which pieces were broken off as a sweetening agent.

clue.text: A drink, say, imbibed by students

indicators.note: something imbibed is drunk in, so it ends up inside the other piece

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students in Britain
eg, for example, is what say means here

explanation.surface: Students knock back a drink, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot mixture of port or sherry with sugar, lemon and spice, an old-fashioned beverage.

clue.text: Secure alarm used by a weight-lifter

definitions.note: the definition describes the item as the thing used, a noun phrase with the item understood

parts.note: to bar a door is to secure it
a bell is an alarm, as in alarm bell

explanation.surface: A weight-lifter rigs up a safety alarm in the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: A long metal rod with discs of weights at each end, lifted in the gym.

clue.text: Money that is raised to get garland

parts.note: L stands for pound, the British unit of money, from Latin libra

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the letters go upwards, so they read in reverse

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Cash is collected to buy a wreath.
explanation.walkthrough: LEI is also Romanian money, a neat false trail for the solver.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hawaiian flower necklace, a wreath worn round the neck.

clue.text: Build viaduct to remedy deficiency

explanation.surface: Engineers construct a viaduct to fix a shortfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, to span a chasm with a structure; figuratively, to make up for a shortfall or close a divide.

clue.text: Sprint along one's regular route

explanation.surface: A runner dashes along the usual circuit they take every day.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash quickly is to race on foot; a round or beat that a milkman or paperboy covers each day is also called this.

clue.text: Fellow embraced by gaudily dressed swimmer

indicators.note: something embraced by another is held within it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: someone gaudily dressed looks garish, loud and showy
F is the standard abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS

explanation.surface: A man is hugged by someone in loud, flashy clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a slender fish with a long beaked snout, so a creature of the water.

clue.text: Hangs on, like the hopeful angler

explanation.surface: Someone waits patiently, as a fisherman does.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for refusing to give way or waiting on the telephone; literally, a fisherman keeps a grip on his tackle.

clue.text: Fops appear as judo expert departs

parts.note: a dan is a grade of black belt in judo, so a holder is an expert
dies is a euphemism for departs this life

explanation.surface: Showy men turn up just as the martial-arts master leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Fops are men overly devoted to smart clothes and appearance, as are these vain dressers.

clue.text: Bobby is distinguished

explanation.surface: A policeman stands out from the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A part-time volunteer police constable in Britain is so called, a bobby being slang for a policeman; it also means exceptional or out of the ordinary.

clue.text: One-time champ given leave-warrant

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-husband
to champ is to chew noisily, that is, to eat

explanation.surface: A former champion is granted permission to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'champ' looks like a winner but is the verb, to munch. An EXEAT is the permission a British boarding school or college gives a pupil to be absent.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a formal permit for temporary absence from school or college, a written pass to go away.

clue.text: Mob British rugby players in control centres

parts.note: a mob is a gang of people
the British and Irish Lions are the touring rugby union side drawn from Britain and Ireland

explanation.surface: A crowd of British rugby players is somehow running headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: These are clusters of nerve cells acting as relay and coordination hubs in the nervous system.

clue.text: Anything but a day centre!

parts.note: a day centre is a place for daytime care; its opposite is a venue for entertainment after dark

explanation.surface: Somewhere definitely not a daytime care facility.
explanation.definitionFit: A late-opening venue for dancing, drinks and shows after dark.

clue.text: Man Arthur used to get good floor covering

parts.note: he stands for a man, the male pronoun

indicators.note: something used is worn or second-hand, so the name's letters have been knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A man called Arthur is employed to fit a decent carpet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' turns ARTHUR into ARTHRU, set between HE and G.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small mat laid in front of the fireplace, a kind of carpet.

clue.text: Tory leader criticised for getting cornered

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: rapped means rebuked or criticised sharply

explanation.surface: A Conservative chief is attacked for being boxed in.
explanation.definitionFit: Caught with no escape, as an animal in a snare.

clue.text: Unexpected problem with locking device

explanation.surface: Something went wrong with the lock.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden snag or drawback is a so-called hitch; a latch or fastening on a door or window is also called this.

clue.text: Welcoming blast of cold air

indicators.note: a blast scatters things, so the letters of the following words are blown into a new order

explanation.surface: A chilly breeze greets you.
explanation.definitionFit: Warm and friendly in manner, hearty and hospitable.

clue.text: They entertain the forces, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: troops are soldiers, the armed forces

explanation.surface: Performers come to amuse the army, so it's said.
explanation.definitionFit: Companies of actors or dancers who perform shows.

clue.text: Poor Olga — hit by a monstrous man

indicators.note: poor here means badly made or in a sorry state, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Unlucky Olga is struck by a huge brute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges the letters of OLGA and HIT.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical Philistine giant slain by David, now a byword for any huge person.

clue.text: Leading man (a pole) gets the bird

parts.note: the hero is the leading man in a story
N is north, one of the two poles

explanation.surface: The star of the show is given a bird by a Pole.
explanation.walkthrough: '(a pole)' looks like a Polish person; it is N, the north pole. 'gets the bird' also suggests being booed.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-legged wading bird of rivers and marshes, grey with a dagger beak.

clue.text: Utter confusion for united marines in work

indicators.note: the first two pieces are placed in the third, which wraps around them

parts.note: toil is hard work
U is a common abbreviation for united, as in football club names
RM stands for Royal Marines

explanation.surface: Total chaos as merged marine units get to work.
explanation.definitionFit: Complete disorder or upheaval, chaos of the highest degree.

clue.text: Adepts get by and succeed

parts.note: adepts are experts, professionals
per means by, as in per post

explanation.surface: Skilled people make ends meet and do well.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrive or flourish financially is to do well.

clue.text: Some codes are written in verse

indicators.note: some of the following word is used, so the letters are hidden inside it

explanation.surface: Certain secret ciphers are composed as poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyric poem addressed to a subject, so a piece of poetry.

clue.text: Peg's credit-card number

explanation.surface: A woman called Peg has her card code.
explanation.definitionFit: A small peg or fastener is this; a personal identification number used with a bank card is also this.

clue.text: They may ring after exchange of rings

definitions.text: They may ring after exchange of rings

parts.words: They may ring after exchange of rings
parts.note: after a couple swap marriage bands, church peals are sounded to celebrate the ceremony

explanation.surface: Something chimes once two people have swapped jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Church peals rung to celebrate a marriage, which follow the swapping of vows and bands.
